deep.reconstruction:
Notation: Π(s)=Γ(s+1) (Gauss); λ(s)=Σ_{n≥1} n^{-s}=ζ(s), so Riemann writes ζ as λ here; 'log n^ν' means (log n)^ν. The page has four blocks.

(A) Singular part of Σ (log n)^ν n^{-1-s} near s=0, i.e. of (−1)^ν ζ^{(ν)}(1+s).
The tail Σ_{n>m} is replaced by the integral from m+1 to ∞. With x=e^t:
∫_{m+1}^∞ (log x)^ν x^{-s-1} dx = ∫_{L}^∞ t^ν e^{-st} dt = Π(ν)/s^{ν+1} − ∫_0^L e^{-st} t^ν dt, where L=log(m+1).
Then −∫_0^L e^{-st}t^ν dt = −∫_0^L (e^{-st}−1)t^ν dt − L^{ν+1}/(ν+1) [split filled in by me]. This gives line 1:
Σ_{2}^{∞} (log n)^ν/n^{s+1} ≈ Σ_{2}^{m} (log n)^ν/n^{s+1} − ∫_0^{log(m+1)} (e^{-st}−1)t^ν dt − (log(m+1))^{ν+1}/(ν+1) + Π(ν)/s^{ν+1}.
The pole term ν!/s^{ν+1} is exactly the principal part of (−1)^ν ζ^{(ν)}(1+s). The remaining terms are regular at s=0. At s=0 the constant is Σ_{n≤m}(log n)^ν/n − (log(m+1))^{ν+1}/(ν+1) + o(1). This is the limit defining the Stieltjes constant γ_ν, although Riemann does not name or isolate it.

Line 2 generalises this to weights (log log n)^m (log n)^ν. Note that m is used both as cutoff and as exponent. The lower limit is 2 because log log 1 is undefined. Using
∫_0^∞ e^{-st} t^ν (log t)^m dt = ∂^m/∂ν^m [Π(ν) s^{-ν-1}] = Σ_μ C(m,μ) (∂^μΠ(ν)/∂ν^μ) (−log s)^{m−μ} s^{-ν-1},
he gets: tail ≈ −∫_0^{log(m+1)} e^{-st} t^ν (log t)^m dt + Σ_μ [(−log s)^{m−μ}/s^{ν+1}] ∂^μΠν/∂ν^μ · Π(m)/(Π(m−μ)Π(μ)).
With ν real (possibly ν=−1, i.e. weights 1/log n), these give the singular behaviour of Dirichlet series with 'prime-density-like' coefficients. This fits the next block on Σp^{-s}.

(B) Prime zeta function and log ζ.
- φ(s) = −Σ_p log(1−p^{-s}) (= log ζ(s)).
- φ'(s) = −Σ_p log p · p^{-s}/(1−p^{-s}) = −Σ_p log p (p^{-s}+p^{-2s}+…).
- With g(s)=Σ_p log p · p^{-s} we have −φ'(s) = Σ_k g(ks). Möbius inversion gives
  −Σ_p log p · p^{-s} = φ'(s) − Σ_p φ'(ps) + Σ_{p<p'} φ'(pp's) − … ('pp, s' = product of two distinct primes).
- Similarly φ(s) = Σ_k P(ks)/k inverts to Σ_p p^{-s} = Σ_q μ(q) φ(qs)/q. This is the Dirichlet-series form of the inversion π(x)=Σμ(n)f(x^{1/n})/n of the 1859 paper.

(C) Functional equation, stated: λ(s) = λ(1−s) Π(−s) (2π)^s sin(sπ/2)/π, i.e. ζ(s)=2^sπ^{s−1}sin(πs/2)Γ(1−s)ζ(1−s).
Mellin representation: Π(s−1)λ(s) = Σ_n ∫_0^∞ e^{-nx}x^{s−1}dx = ∫_0^∞ x^{s−1}/(e^x−1) dx.
There is also a scrap of the partial-fraction formula 1/f(x) = Σ_α 1/((x−α)f'(α)) for simple zeros α; the rest of that line is illegible.

(D) Proof of the functional equation by partial fractions.
1. From sin x = x Π(1−x²/n²π²): cot x = 1/x − Σ 2x/((1−x²/n²π²)n²π²).
2. Then e^{-ix}/sin x = cot x − i = 2i/(e^{2ix}−1).
3. Putting y=2ix: 2/(e^y−1) = −1 + 2/y + Σ_n y/((1+y²/4n²π²)n²π²), i.e. 1/(e^y−1) = 1/y − 1/2 + Σ 2y/(y²+4n²π²).
4. Loop integral (as in the 1859 paper): 2i sin(πs) Π(s−1) λ(s) = −∫_loop (−x)^{s−1} dx/(e^x−1).
5. Insert the partial fractions. The −1 and 2/x terms are silently dropped (formal for Re s<0). This gives −Σ_n ∫ (−x)^{s−1} 2x dx/((1+x²/4n²π²)4n²π²).
6. Scale x → 2nπx in each term: = −∫ (−x)^{s−1} 2x dx/(1+x²) · Σ(2nπ)^{s−1} = −(2π)^{s−1} λ(1−s) ∫_loop (−x)^{s−1} 2x dx/(1+x²).
7. Return to the real axis (cancelling 2i sin πs) and substitute y=x²:
   Π(s−1)λ(s) = (2π)^{s−1}λ(1−s) ∫_0^∞ y^{(s−1)/2} dy/(1+y) = λ(1−s)(2π)^{s−1} Π((s−1)/2) Π((−s−1)/2),
   using ∫_0^∞ y^{a−1}/(1+y) dy = Γ(a)Γ(1−a) = π/cos(πs/2) with a=(s+1)/2.
8. Legendre duplication, written as λ(s)(2π)^{-1/2} 2^{s+1/2} Π(s/2) Π((s−1)/2), plus an auxiliary line 2^sΠ(s/2)Π((s−1)/2)/Π(s) = … √π. Dividing gives the symmetric form
   λ(s) Π(s/2−1) π^{−s/2} = λ(1−s) Π((1−s)/2−1) π^{(s−1)/2},
   i.e. π^{−s/2}Γ(s/2)ζ(s) is invariant under s→1−s.
9. Struck fragments π/sin((1−s)/2·π) and (2π)^{s−1} are remnants of using the reflection formula.

Overall: a reworking of the two proofs of the functional equation from the 1859 memoir, by a partial-fraction/scaling route instead of residues. It is preceded by Euler–Maclaurin-type isolation of the singular parts at s=1 of ζ^{(ν)} and of log-log-weighted series, and by Möbius inversion linking Σp^{-s} with log ζ.
errors: Lines 1–2 are written with '=' but are only approximations: the tail sum Σ_{n>m} is replaced by ∫_{m+1}^∞ without Euler–Maclaurin corrections. The difference is O(f(m+1)) and analytic near s=0, so the formulas are correct as m→∞ or modulo regular terms, but not as exact identities.
In line 1 the term (log(m+1))^{ν+1}/(ν+1) breaks down at ν=−1, where a log log term is needed; line 2 handles that case.
Line 2 uses m both as the summation cutoff and as the exponent of log log n (notational clash, not a mathematical error).

Line '(cos x + i sin x)/sin x = −i + 1/x − Σ…': with '+' the left side equals cot x + i, not cot x − i. The next line (2i e^{-ix}/(e^{ix}−e^{-ix})) shows the intended numerator is cos x − i sin x = e^{-ix}. So either the sign is misread or it is a slip.

Step 5 drops the −1 and 2/x terms of the partial-fraction expansion inside the loop integral. Their loop integrals ∫(−x)^{s−1}dx diverge for every s, so this is formal (zero by analytic-continuation regularisation). Interchanging sum and integral is also unjustified as written; the rigorous version is Riemann's own residue argument for Re s<0.

The duplication step reads Π(s−1)λs = λs(2π)^{-1/2}2^{s+1/2}Π(s/2)Π((s−1)/2). But 2^sπ^{-1/2}Π(s/2)Π((s−1)/2) = Π(s), not Π(s−1); the correct factor is Π(s/2−1) (or 2^{s−1}π^{-1/2}Π(s/2)…/(s/2)). This is an index slip, and the final symmetric formula correctly uses Π(s/2−1).
The auxiliary line 2^sΠ(s/2)Π((s−1)/2)/Π(s) should equal √π. The RHS as transcribed ('2π^{1/2}/… Π(s−1)') is partly struck and does not match unless read differently.

results.what: Isolation of the principal part ν!/s^{ν+1} of Σ(log n)^ν n^{-1-s} at s=0 by comparing the tail sum with an integral; the regular part at s=0 is lim[Σ_{n≤m}(log n)^ν/n − (log m)^{ν+1}/(ν+1)]
results.modern_name: Laurent expansion of ζ at s=1 / Stieltjes constants γ_ν (implicit)
results.usually_credited_to: Stieltjes (1885 letter to Hermite), Jensen (1887); Euler–Maclaurin method generally

results.what: Singular behaviour at s=0 of Σ (log log n)^m (log n)^ν n^{-1-s}: Σ_μ C(m,μ) Γ^{(μ)}(ν+1)(−log s)^{m−μ}/s^{ν+1}, via ∂^m/∂ν^m of Γ(ν+1)s^{-ν-1}
results.modern_name: Mellin/Laplace transform asymptotics of log-power weights (Tauberian-type singularity analysis)
results.usually_credited_to: standard 19th-c. technique (Landau-era analytic number theory systematised such expansions)

results.what: Σ_p p^{-s} = Σ_q μ(q) log ζ(qs)/q and −Σ_p log p p^{-s} = Σ μ(k) φ'(ks)
results.modern_name: Möbius inversion for the prime zeta function
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1859 (equivalent form for π(x)); prime zeta form often attributed to Glaisher 1891 / Landau

results.modern_name: Functional equation of the Riemann zeta function; Mellin integral representation

results.what: Partial fractions cot x = 1/x − Σ2x/(n²π²−x²) and 1/(e^x−1) = 1/x − 1/2 + Σ2x/(x²+4n²π²)
results.modern_name: Mittag-Leffler / Euler partial fraction expansion of cot and Bose kernel

results.what: Derivation of the functional equation by inserting the partial fractions of 1/(e^x−1) into the loop integral, scaling each term to ∫(−x)^{s−1}2x dx/(1+x²), and evaluating ∫_0^∞y^{a−1}/(1+y)dy = Γ(a)Γ(1−a)
results.modern_name: Partial-fraction (scaling) proof of the zeta functional equation
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1859 (residue version); the scaling variant appears in later textbook expositions

results.what: Symmetric form π^{−s/2}Γ(s/2)ζ(s) = π^{−(1−s)/2}Γ((1−s)/2)ζ(1−s) via Legendre duplication

deep.surprise_reason: Most of the page re-derives the functional equation and the Möbius inversion of log ζ, both in or immediately equivalent to the 1859 memoir; the partial-fraction scaling route is only a mild variant. The mildly notable part is the opening: a systematic extraction of the principal parts at s=1 of ζ^{(ν)} and of log-log-weighted Dirichlet series, including Γ-derivative/(−log s) terms. This implicitly contains the limit formula for the Stieltjes constants about two decades before Stieltjes and Jensen, but without isolating or naming them.

transcription_corrections: 'log n^ν' throughout means (log n)^ν; '(log m+1)' and 'log m+1' mean log(m+1); 'log t^m' means (log t)^m.
In line 1 the struck fragment is a cancelled attempt; the surviving terms are −∫_0^{log(m+1)}(e^{-st}−1)t^ν dt − (log(m+1))^{ν+1}/(ν+1) + Πν/s^{ν+1}.
'−log p Σ' 1/p^s + 1/p^{2s}' should be read as −Σ_p log p (p^{-s}+p^{-2s}+…).
'−log Π 1/p^s = …' is better read as −Σ log p · 1/p^s = φ'(s) − Σφ'(ps) + Σφ'(pp's) (Möbius inversion), not a product.
'Σ [?] φ(qs)/q': the illegible symbol is the Möbius sign factor (±1 or 0 according to q), i.e. Σ μ(q)φ(qs)/q.
'lg(1−x²/n²π²)' needs a summation sign: log sin x = log x + Σ log(1−x²/n²π²).
'(cos x + sin x i)/sin x' is presumably (cos x − i sin x)/sin x (= e^{-ix}/sin x), consistent with the RHS −i + cot x and the next line.
The illegible line '= Σ r^{∂ log s} ϱ^{σα}' is uncertain and could not be verified from the image.
Bottom-left: the line reads 2^{s}Π(s/2)Π((s−1)/2)/Π s = … with partly struck right side involving π^{1/2}; the correct value is √π.
